description: Race results are the component entries of a race; an entry cannot exist without the race it belongs to.
Qualifying records are component parts of the race weekend they belong to.
Lap records are component parts of the race in which the laps were driven.
A race result is one component of a driver's participation record; it has no meaning without its driver.
A race result names exactly one constructor as a component of the entry.
A qualifying record names exactly one constructor as a component of the entry.
A season is composed of the races scheduled in its year; a race cannot exist outside a season.

connection_condition: races.circuitId corresponds to circuits.circuitId; the connection is indirect in that a race is hosted at a circuit rather than made of one
description: A race is hosted at a circuit. A race is not a kind of circuit and is not composed of one, so the relationship is a host association.
The full name of a driver is derived by concatenating the driver's forename and surname in that order.
Age is computed from the date of birth relative to a reference date; the youngest driver therefore has the maximum date of birth and the oldest has the minimum.
The fastest lap time of an entry is the minimum of that entry's individual lap times, the same quantity that is also stored per entry in results.fastestLapTime.
The fastest lap number is the lap ordinal at which the entry's minimum lap time was set.
The race winner is the entry whose finishing position is 1 in that race.
The season champion is the driver or constructor holding championship position 1 in the standings after the final race of the season.

connection_condition: an entry's completion is visible both in its results.time and in its finishing status, and the two usually agree because statusId 1 means 'Finished'
description: Status and completion describe the same outcome from two angles: whether the entry ran to the end and why it did not.
A completion rate is derived by dividing the number of completed entries by the total entries in scope and expressing the result as a percentage.

connection_condition: nationality is an attribute column on the driver row rather than a reference to a country table
description: A driver has a nationality recorded as a demonym string; there is no country dimension table to join.

connection_condition: nationality is an attribute column on the constructor row
description: A constructor has a nationality recorded as a demonym string drawn from the same vocabulary as driver nationality.

connection_condition: country is an attribute column on the circuit row
description: A circuit lies in a country recorded as a plain country name on the circuit row.

connection_condition: drivers.driverRef and drivers.code are two columns of the same drivers row
description: The reference name and the three-letter code are alternative identifiers for the same driver, asked for interchangeably as 'reference name' or 'abbreviated code'.

connection_condition: the constructor of the winning entry is the value of results.constructorId on the row whose position is 1
description: A race winner drives for a constructor, so a question about the constructor of a race champion is answered from the winning entry's constructor reference.

connection_condition: both are accumulated per season in the standings tables and both are also derivable entry by entry from results
description: Wins and points are the two correlated championship measures, accumulated over the same season standings.

connection_condition: only the winning entry carries a total race duration in results.time, so the value identifies the winner
description: The recorded total race time distinguishes the winner from the rest of the field, whose times are gaps.

connection_condition: the classification position orders the drivers whose segment times are recorded on the same qualifying row
description: The qualifying classification summarises the segment times of the same qualifying record.
